content_units: End-of-Term Notice Position for a Cardiff Fixed-Term AST

For a   12-month AST in Wales   running from   2025-09-01 to 2026-08-31  , with   no break clause   and the tenant leaving   exactly on the last day of the fixed term  , the tenant will   typically not need to give formal notice to end the tenancy on 2026-08-31  , because the fixed term ends automatically on that date if the tenant moves out and returns possession.

A prudent tenant should still give the landlord/agent   written advance confirmation   of the move-out date to avoid confusion, re-letting disputes, and deposit arguments. A common low-friction approach is   about 1 month’s written notice as a courtesy  , even where not legally required.
Wales-Specific Notice and Move-Out Checklist
Item   Typical position for this scenario   Why it matters   What to check
Fixed term end     Ends on 2026-08-31     Tenancy usually ends automatically if tenant leaves on time   Tenancy agreement start/end dates

Tenant notice to leave on final day     Usually not legally required   for fixed-term expiry   Avoids accidental rollover into periodic tenancy only if tenant actually vacates   Any clause requiring notice at fixed-term end
Rent cycle   Monthly   Relevant if tenancy rolls into periodic occupation after 2026-08-31   Rent due date and payment period wording
Break clause   None   Tenant cannot end early through a contractual break route   Whole tenancy agreement
Holding over risk   Staying past end date can create a periodic tenancy or liability issues   May trigger need for notice later and extra rent exposure   Keys return date; actual vacation date

Cardiff, Wales rules   Welsh renting law may affect occupation contracts, notices, and paperwork terminology   Some landlords/agents still use AST language loosely   Whether contract converted/is treated under Renting Homes (Wales) framework
Documents That Matter Most
Check these in this order:
-   Written tenancy agreement / occupation contract
- Confirm the   fixed term end date: 2026-08-31  .
- Look for any clause saying the tenant must give notice   even at the end of the fixed term  .
- Check clauses on   key return  ,   cleaning  ,   carpets  ,   gardens  ,   professional cleaning  , and   check-out process  .
-   Deposit protection paperwork
- Confirm which scheme protects the deposit and the   prescribed information   / scheme terms.
- Review the scheme’s evidence standards for cleaning, damage, rent arrears, and missing items.
-   Inventory and check-in report
- This is usually the most important dispute document.
- Compare current condition against the signed move-in inventory, photos, meter readings, and listed contents.
-   Any renewal or variation documents
- Make sure no later agreement changed the original fixed term or added a notice requirement.
-   Agent/landlord emails and letters
- Check whether they previously asked for a certain amount of notice or a specific check-out method.
- Written communication can help show cooperation if a dispute later arises.
Steps That Best Protect the Deposit
Option 1:   Give clear written move-out confirmation now     Short email confirming you will vacate on   2026-08-31   and return all keys that day   Reduces argument about notice/overholding
Draft email
Option 2:   Prepare evidence against deductions     Clean thoroughly, photograph every room, appliances, meters, and outside areas on departure day   Strongest practical protection for deposit
Deposit help
Option 3:   Use a documented key handover     Return keys by receipt, office log, or timestamped message/photo   Helps prove possession ended on time
Check Welsh guidance

Option 4:   Compare move-in vs move-out condition carefully     Aim for cleanliness and condition consistent with the inventory, allowing for fair wear and tear   Reduces exaggerated cleaning/damage claims
Deposit disputes
Low-Dispute Exit Plan for 2026-08-31
- Send a   written confirmation email   to the landlord/agent around   late July or early August 2026   saying:
- you will vacate on   31 August 2026
- you will return all keys that day
- you want check-out instructions and deposit return process details
- Before leaving:
- remove all belongings
- clean kitchen, bathroom, appliances, windows you are responsible for, and bins
- restore any agreed changes if required by the contract
- take   dated photos/videos   of every room and item
- take   final gas/electric/water meter readings
- On move-out day:
- return keys exactly as instructed
- get written confirmation of receipt
- keep proof of checkout communication
- Right after move-out:
- email forwarding address, bank details if needed, photos, and meter readings
- ask for the deposit return timetable in writing
Practical Context for This Scenario

Because the property is in   Cardiff, Wales  , terminology may differ from older England-and-Wales AST guidance, especially after Welsh housing law reforms. In practice, the safest route is:   do not rely only on the general rule  —check the contract wording and give clear written confirmation anyway.
This is especially important because some agreements or agent processes try to impose operational steps even where the tenancy is simply ending by expiry of the fixed term.
